newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina should stay with peso parity - laureates.
newsitem.headline: Argentina should stay with peso parity - laureates.

text.p: Two Nobel laureates in economics, Gary Becker and Robert Lucas, recommended Argentina stick to its Convertibility Plan that pegs the peso at par with the dollar, newspapers reported Tuesday.

"You have to carry on that path (Convertibility) because you cannot rule out that someone be sufficiently stupid to return to hyperinflation," said Lucas, who won the Nobel in 1995, during a short visit to Buenos Aires.
Lucas said he liked Convertibility because it took away the foreign exchange policy "from the hands of the politicians."
Becker, who concentrated his comments on the need for Argentina to promote freer labor markets, said that current unemployment of 17 percent was not a result of peso parity.
"The reasons for that problem (unemployment) are the recession that Argentina went through recently. And the other cause is the rigidity of labor markets," said Becker.
Argentine President Carlos Menem is currently leading a drive to pass more flexible labor laws.
Becker said he remembered Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez from his days as a University of Chicago graduate student and said he was "excellent."
